findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 31 mm is observed in the head of the pancreas. Retropancreatic tissue invasion is noted. There is contact of more than 180° with both the portal vein and the superior mesenteric vein, along with vascular stenosis, suggesting invasion. No invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum is observed. Contact of more than 180° with the common hepatic artery is observed, suggesting invasion, though the tumor does not involve the proper hepatic artery or celiac artery. No other local invasion factors are identified. Lymph node metastases are observed in one node at station 12a and three nodes at station 12b. No other evident metastases are observed.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH1 (contact with common hepatic artery), DU0 (no invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum), S1 (retropancreatic tissue invasion), RP1 (vascular stenosis and invasion of portal vein and superior mesenteric vein), PV1 (contact of more than 180° with portal vein), A1 (contact of more than 180° with common hepatic artery), PL0 (no invasion of proper hepatic artery or celiac artery), OO0 (no other local invasion factors identified).

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the size of the tumor (31 mm) and the local invasion factors identified, the T classification is T3.

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer are defined as follows:
- Head: 12a, 12b, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17
- Body: 8a, 8b, 9, 10, 11
- Tail: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7

The patient's metastatic lymph node stations are 12a and 12b. These are regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer located in the head of the pancreas. Counting only the metastatic lymph nodes within the regional stations, there are 4 involved regional nodes (1 at station 12a and 3 at station 12b). Therefore, the N classification is N1b.

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

There are no distant metastases observed, so the M classification is M0.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the results of Task 1 and Task 4, the tumor is not unresectable due to distant or non-regional metastasis, and there are no other criteria for borderline resectable or unresectable. Therefore, the resectability classification is Resectable (R).

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the determined T (T3), N (N1b), and M (M0) categories, the overall stage is Stage IIB.
